年内最贵新股频准激光上市，募资总额
18.69亿元
8月18日，年内最贵新股频准激光在科创板正式挂牌，其发行价定为186.88元/股，单签500股缴款金额高达93440元，刷新2026年A股新股申购资金门槛纪录。本次合计发行1000万股新股，发行后总股本4000万股，整体募资总额18.69亿元，扣除各类发行费用后实际募集资金净额17.25亿元。本次募资将投入精准激光产业化、武汉研发中心、总部研发基地三大项目，同时补充流动资金，持续扩产叠加研发迭代巩固份额。

IBM连接并运行两个模块化低温系统，推进容错量子计算
8月19日，IBM连接并冷却了两个模块化低温系统，作为其构建可扩展基础设施以支持更大型容错量子计算机的努力之一。这两个模块在五天内冷却至4开尔文后，电流降至15毫开尔文以下，并扩展了量子处理器连接的布线容量。IBM计划使用L耦合器连接多个处理器，目标到2027年至少达到1000个可编程量子比特，并计划2029年部署于IBM Quantum Starling。

中国在量子技术国际标准领域取得新进展
8月17日，中国国家市场监管总局表示，中国在量子技术国际标准领域取得新进展。在山东省济南市召开的国际标准组织量子技术联合技术委员会第五次全体会议期间，由中国牵头的《量子熵源随机性质量和测试方法学的概述和分析》国际标准提案正式获批立项，这也标志着中国在量子核心器件国际标准制定中迈出重要一步。

8月18日，NTT DOCOMO宣布已部署其第二个基于D-Wave的量子计算应用，用于优化移动网络区域列表的跟踪。该应用在一个具有代表性的网络优化问题中，将峰值位置注册信号降低了65.3%，分页信号减少了7.0%。该系统在大约五分钟内优化了覆盖333个基站、3个预备区列表和9个跟踪区域的问题，并将结果纳入网络规划和运营中。

美国北卡罗来纳州立大学等研究动力学平均场论的高效量子实现
本研究致力于在量子计算机上实现动力学平均场理论（
DMFT）的计算框架，重点关注近期的实际应用。研究利用杂质问题的结构特性，将基态的低秩高斯子空间表示与经过压缩的浅层量子电路相结合，该电路融合了态制备与时间演化功能，用以计算格林函数。研究在无噪声环境下展示了基于高斯子空间的DMFT算法收敛性，并在IBM量子处理器上通过提取单个杂质耦合三个浴轨道（8个量子比特，1个辅助比特）的杂质格林函数，验证了电路压缩的硬件可行性。研究成果于8月17日发表于《
npj Computational Materials
》（
npj计算材料学）。

英国牛津大学等研究超导量子比特阵列中的串扰色散与空间标度
本研究建立了超导
transmon晶格中相邻及非相邻量子比特残余串扰的统一理论和实验框架，揭示了耦合强度随空间距离的指数衰减和随频率失谐的依赖关系，并在4×4量子比特阵列上验证了4-6GHz范围内所有最近邻耦合的标度律。研究表明，忽略空间和谱依赖的标准色散近似会系统性高估长程串扰，该框架为大规模量子处理器中的串扰抑制提供了设计指导。研究成果于8月17日发表于《Physical Review Research》（物理评论研究）。

https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/2zb3-4vwq
美国太平洋西北国家实验室等研究基于校准条件特征线性调制解码器
本研究提出硬件条件神经解码器，利用超导处理器校准与解码时间尺度分离的特性，通过校准数据调控轻量级神经网络，兼顾重型校准处理与低延迟解码。在
IBM重复码实验（超270万次测试，码距达11）中，该模型无需重训即可泛化至新比特链和新校准数据。相比改进的完美匹配算法，逻辑错误率最大降低11.1倍，且延迟开销极低。这表明硬件感知、校准自适应的神经解码是面向实际容错计算的高效方案。研究成果于8月17日发表于《Physical Review Research》（物理评论研究）。

## Research Papers

### North Carolina State University et al. Study Efficient Quantum Implementation of Dynamical Mean-Field Theory

This work aims to implement a computational framework for dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) on quantum computers, with a focus on near-term practical applications. The study leverages the structural properties of the impurity problem, combining a low-rank Gaussian subspace representation of the ground state with compressed shallow quantum circuits that integrate state preparation and time evolution to compute Green's functions. The research demonstrates convergence of the Gaussian-subspace-based DMFT algorithm in a noise-free setting and validates the hardware feasibility of circuit compression on an IBM quantum processor by extracting the impurity Green's function for a single impurity coupled to three bath orbitals (8 qubits, 1 ancilla qubit). Published August 17 in *npj Computational Materials*.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-026-02289-2

### University of Oxford et al. Study Crosstalk Dispersion and Spatial Scaling in Superconducting Qubit Arrays

This work establishes a unified theoretical and experimental framework for residual crosstalk between nearest-neighbor and non-nearest-neighbor qubits in superconducting transmon lattices, revealing exponential decay of coupling strength with spatial distance and its dependence on frequency detuning. The scaling laws were validated for all nearest-neighbor couplings in the 4–6 GHz range on a 4×4 qubit array. The study demonstrates that the standard dispersive approximation, which neglects spatial and spectral dependence, systematically overestimates long-range crosstalk, and provides design guidelines for crosstalk suppression in large-scale quantum processors. Published August 17 in *Physical Review Research*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/2zb3-4vwq

### Pacific Northwest National Laboratory et al. Study Calibration-Conditioned Linear-Feature Neural Decoders

This work proposes hardware-conditioned neural decoders that exploit the timescale separation between superconducting processor calibration and decoding, using calibration data to modulate lightweight neural networks to balance heavy calibration processing with low-latency decoding. The model generalizes to new qubit chains and new calibration data without retraining, demonstrated on IBM repetition-code experiments (over 2.7 million trials, code distances up to 11). Compared to an improved minimum-weight perfect matching algorithm, logical error rates were reduced by up to 11.1× with minimal latency overhead, demonstrating that hardware-aware, calibration-adaptive neural decoding is an efficient approach for practical fault-tolerant computation. Published August 17 in *Physical Review Research*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/ftdh-t3yg

### Sandia National Laboratories Proposes Frequency Beam Splitter Design Based on Coupled Resonator Modulation Arrays

This work proposes a frequency beam splitter design based on coupled resonator modulation arrays and constructs its effective transfer matrix using the SLH formalism. The approach is flexible and composable, supporting the definition of N-mode beam splitters or networks interconnected from l-mode devices. The method is applied to analyze dual/quad-resonator devices, frequency-domain phase shifters, and Mach–Zehnder interferometers, and a no-go theorem is derived prohibiting a subclass of N-mode frequency-domain beam splitters from being natively implemented with an N-resonator array. Published August 17 in *Physical Review Applied*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prapplied/abstract/10.1103/7jm4-641d

### Cornell University et al. Study Krypton-Sputtered Tantalum Thin Films for Scalable High-Performance Quantum Devices

This work demonstrates that switching the sputtering gas from argon to krypton promotes the synthesis of body-centered cubic (BCC) phase tantalum thin films on silicon substrates at temperatures as low as 200°C, providing a broad process window compatible with back-end-of-line manufacturing standards. Coplanar waveguide resonators fabricated from krypton-sputtered films exhibit excellent and compact microwave performance distributions. Films grown at higher temperatures show increased loss correlated with interdiffusion at the tantalum–silicon interface. Transmon qubits with compact 20 μm capacitor gaps fabricated from these films demonstrate quality factors of up to 16.9 million. Published August 18 in *Nature Materials*.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-026-02718-z#author-information

### University of Cambridge et al. Prove Kirkwood–Dirac Non-Positivity Is a Necessary Resource for Quantum Computing

This work examines the boundary between classical and quantum computation from the perspective of quantum resource theory, proving that the non-positivity of the Kirkwood–Dirac (KD) quasi-probability distribution is a necessary resource for achieving quantum computational advantage. The study represents quantum circuits implemented via surface-code defect braiding as KD quasi-probability distributions and finds that when this distribution remains positive throughout the computation, the circuit can be efficiently simulated by a classical algorithm. Bound magic states with non-stabilizer properties that remain efficiently classically simulable are also constructed. The work further proves that KD non-positivity is a resource monotone in this model, providing a new theoretical framework for characterizing the non-classical resources required for quantum computational advantage. Published August 18 in *Physical Review Letters*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/x819-898d

### University of Innsbruck et al. Propose Gaussian Process Models for Noise-Robust Optimization of Variational Quantum Algorithms

This work addresses the difficulty of optimizing variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) under noisy measurement conditions, proposing specialized trigonometric-kernel Gaussian process models suited to quantum cost functions. Exploiting the fact that VQA cost functions typically contain only a small number of oscillation frequencies, the study systematically compares different kernel functions on quantum chemistry and combinatorial optimization tasks, and further develops the RotoGP sequential line-search optimizer based on the Gaussian process model. Results show that the trigonometric kernel performs best in most tests, effectively mitigating measurement noise and improving optimization convergence, providing a new approach for VQA optimization on noisy quantum devices. Published August 18 in *Physical Review Research*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/p947-r9l1

### RIKEN (理化学研究所) Proposes General Parallel Algorithm Based on OR-Represented Quantum Algebra

This work proposes a general parallel algorithm based on OR-represented quantum algebra (ORQA) for classical simulation of large-scale quantum many-body dynamics and quantum circuits. The method applies to arbitrary spin systems and can be combined with quantum circuit simulation in the Heisenberg picture. The researchers simulated a 127-qubit heavy-hexagonal lattice kicked Ising model on the Fugaku supercomputer, tracking the evolution of up to 10¹² Pauli strings with large-scale parallel scalability. The work provides a high-performance computing tool for experimental validation of large-scale quantum processors and quantum–classical hybrid simulation. Published August 18 in *Physical Review Applied*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prapplied/abstract/10.1103/y8ft-m61w

### Harvard University et al. Achieve Imaginary-Time Evolution and Ground-State Preparation via Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols

This work addresses the problem of low-energy ground-state preparation in quantum computing and quantum simulation, proposing deterministic unitary protocols that implement imaginary-time evolution using multi-copy systems. The approach combines real-time evolution of the system Hamiltonian with controlled-SWAP operations, designing two classes of quantum circuits — tree-type and compact — that offer different trade-offs between resource overhead and preparation fidelity. Numerical results show that mid-circuit post-selection can further accelerate convergence and enables resource exchange between circuit depth and number of measurements. The work provides new algorithmic pathways for efficient ground-state preparation and hybrid simulation on near-term quantum platforms. Published August 18 in *PRX Quantum*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prxquantum/abstract/10.1103/1tf6-bc55

### Pasqal et al. Study Thousand-Atom-Scale Defect-Free Arrays in a 4 K Cryogenic Environment

This work develops a large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing platform operating at 4 K, integrating high-numerical-aperture optics and compatible with Rydberg-state manipulation. Atom trapping lifetimes were extended to approximately 5,000 seconds; combined with dual-wavelength trapping lasers and loss suppression during atom rearrangement and imaging, defect-free arrays of up to 1,024 atoms were achieved. These results improve both the preparation scale and experimental duration of large-scale neutral-atom arrays, providing hardware foundations for analog and digital quantum computing. Published August 18 in *PRX Quantum*.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prxquantum/abstract/10.1103/45t1-vl5y

### BITS Pilani (印度皮拉尼比尔拉理工学院) Uses Bravyi–Kitaev Transformation to Solve Two-Mode Master Equations

This work explores digital simulation of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians derived via the thermofield dynamics approach on quantum computers. The Hamiltonian is mapped to qubits via the Bravyi–Kitaev transformation, and time evolution is approximated using Suzuki–Trotter decompositions of different orders. Quantum circuits are constructed and compared against exact solutions; convergence is analyzed by extracting the lowest real-part quasi-energy of the evolution operator, showing that higher-order Trotterization improves accuracy at the cost of increased circuit depth. The work provides a concrete scheme for digital simulation of open quantum systems. Published August 19 in *Scientific Reports*.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-64213-4

### Sharif University of Technology (伊朗谢里夫理工大学) Studies Parallel Data Processing in Quantum Machine Learning

This work proposes a quantum machine learning (QML) framework that exploits core quantum algorithmic principles — superposition, oracles, and interference — to accelerate training. By encoding training samples as superposition states, processing them through parameterized circuits, and classifying via an interferometer module, the complexity of loss function evaluation is reduced from O(N²) to O(N). Numerical simulations (N ≤ 128) demonstrate that the method reduces the number of circuit executions per cost evaluation from N to 1, achieving a nearly N-fold reduction in quantum overhead while maintaining classification accuracy. The work demonstrates the scalable potential of quantum algorithmic design principles for efficient QML. Published August 19 in *Scientific Reports*.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-65756-2

### VIT Vellore (印度韦洛尔理工大学) Uses Hybrid Quantum-Inspired Differential Evolution to Improve Single-Pixel Adversarial Attacks

This work systematically compares the performance of differential evolution (DE) and hybrid quantum-inspired differential evolution in single-pixel adversarial attacks. Experiments were conducted on CIFAR-10/100 datasets using three CNN architectures (SimpleCNN, ResNet-32, VGG-like), with metrics including success rate, confidence reduction, query count, and computational cost. Results show that hybrid quantum-inspired differential evolution achieves 7–13% higher average confidence reduction than DE but incurs 1.6–1.9× higher computational cost. The study provides guidance on the efficiency–effectiveness trade-off for adversarial attacks in resource-constrained environments. Published August 19 in *Scientific Reports*.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-63261-0
